_note: Auditor-calibration pairs. Each has ONE deliberately planted confound that its 'intended_difference' does not admit. They are shown to the confound auditors only (never to the judging panel) to measure whether auditors catch a real confound. Added after the prior-art check (a published model judge accepted about twice as many items as experts).

pairs.planted_confound: Outcome severity differs: the vestry is flooded and the carpet, piano and records ruined (A) versus a little water drips on the floor (B).
pairs.title: The church boiler
pairs.version_a: Ruth looks after the heating in a small church. On Sunday she notices that the boiler's pressure valve is working loose. She knows that if the valve fails the boiler will overheat and crack, and that tightening it takes one turn of a lever. She wants the church committee to buy a new boiler. She turns the lever the other way, loosening the valve completely, and goes home. That night the boiler overheats and cracks, and hot water floods the vestry, ruining the carpet, the piano and the parish records.
pairs.version_b: Ruth looks after the heating in a small church. On Sunday she notices that the boiler's pressure valve is working loose. She knows that if the valve fails the boiler will overheat and crack, and that tightening it takes one turn of a lever. She wants the church committee to buy a new boiler. She leaves the lever alone and goes home. That night the boiler overheats and cracks, and a little water drips onto the vestry floor.
pairs.intended_difference: Ruth loosens the valve herself (A) versus leaves the loose valve alone (B).
pairs.judgment_question: How morally wrong was Ruth's behavior?
pairs.comprehension_question: What did Ruth want the church committee to do?

pairs.planted_confound: Karl's physical contribution differs: he draws 400 of the 500 litres (A) versus 250 (B).
pairs.title: The rainwater tank
pairs.version_a: Two neighbours, Ida and Karl, share a rainwater tank that holds 500 litres. The housing association's rule is that only ground-floor tenants may draw water from it. Ida lives on the ground floor; Karl lives upstairs. On Saturday Ida drew 100 litres for her vegetables and Karl drew 400 litres for his balcony plants. On Sunday the caretaker needed water to mix cement and found the tank empty.
pairs.version_b: Two neighbours, Ida and Karl, share a rainwater tank that holds 500 litres. The housing association's rule is that all tenants may draw water from it. Ida lives on the ground floor; Karl lives upstairs. On Saturday Ida drew 250 litres for her vegetables and Karl drew 250 litres for his balcony plants. On Sunday the caretaker needed water to mix cement and found the tank empty.
pairs.intended_difference: Karl is not allowed to draw water from the tank (A) versus is allowed to (B).
pairs.judgment_question: How much did Karl cause the tank to be empty?

pairs.planted_confound: The quality of Lena's evidence differs: the café's own website (A) versus a stranger's passing remark (B).
pairs.title: The café's opening time
pairs.version_a: Lena is meeting a client at a café she has never visited. Yesterday she looked up its opening hours on the café's own website, which said it opens at 8:00. She tells the client, “It opens at 8.” The website is kept up to date by the owner, and the café does open at 8:00.
pairs.version_b: Lena is meeting a client at a café she has never visited. Yesterday a stranger on the bus mentioned in passing that he thought it opens at 8:00. She tells the client, “It opens at 8.” The stranger was thinking of a different café with a similar name, but as it happens this café does open at 8:00.
pairs.intended_difference: Lena's belief is true in the normal way (A) versus true only by coincidence (B).
pairs.judgment_question: How much do you agree with this statement: Lena knows that the café opens at 8:00.
